documents.name: incident-response.md
documents.content:
# Incident response

## Severity levels

A sev-1 incident means customer-facing loss of service. A sev-2 incident means degraded service with a workaround. A sev-3 incident is anything else.

## Acknowledgement

A sev-1 incident must be acknowledged within fifteen minutes of the page. A sev-2 incident must be acknowledged within one hour. The on-call engineer acknowledges the page in the incident channel so that everyone can see who is responding.

## Escalation

If the on-call engineer does not acknowledge the page, the secondary on-call engineer is paged after ten minutes. If the secondary does not respond either, the incident commander is paged after twenty minutes. Escalation does not replace acknowledgement: the person who takes the page still has to say so in the channel.

## Communication

While a sev-1 incident is open, the incident commander posts an update every thirty minutes. Customers are informed through the status page rather than through the incident channel.

## Review

Every sev-1 incident requires a written review within five working days. The review records what failed, what was done to restore service, and which follow-up actions were created. The reliability lead tracks those actions until they are closed.

documents.name: encryption-policy.md
documents.content:
# Encryption policy

## Data at rest

Customer data is encrypted at rest with KMS customer managed keys. Keys are rotated annually, and a key is never shared between environments.

## Credential rotation

Database credentials rotate every ninety days through Secrets Manager. Application secrets rotate every one hundred and eighty days. Rotation is automatic and does not require a deployment.

documents.name: access-control.md
documents.content:
# Access control

## Least privilege

Access is granted to a role rather than to a person, and a role carries only the permissions its tasks need. Standing access to production is limited to the platform team.

## Production access

Access to production data is approved by the service owner and expires after eight hours. Every session is logged.

## Reviews

Role assignments are reviewed every quarter. A reviewer confirms each assignment is still needed and removes the ones that are not.

documents.name: backup-restore.md
documents.content:
# Backup and restore

## Snapshots

Every database is snapshotted nightly. Snapshots are retained for thirty-five days, and the newest snapshot is copied to a second region every week.

## Restores

A restore drill runs once a quarter against a scratch database. The drill is not considered complete until an engineer has restored the data and queried it.

documents.name: change-management.md
documents.content:
# Change management

## Deployments

A deployment needs a green build and one review. Deployments run during business hours unless an incident requires otherwise.

## Rollback

Every deployment is rollback-safe: the previous version stays available until the new one has served traffic for an hour. A rollback is a decision, not an escalation, and the engineer who deployed may perform it.
